answer: An agent marketplace can require each account to post a bond that is slashed when independent audits prove it copied another agent’s work or coordinated identities to farm rewards. Audits sample tasks and compare provenance, not just writing style: a mirror-like match across supposedly separate agents triggers review, while a grove of accounts sharing one funder can be treated as one claimant. The umber cost is capital locked per identity, so creating many Sybils multiplies both the bond requirement and the risk of losing it.
